ive been thinking something like this for a while now. ranks dont mean anything. having safety settings for ranks does nothing, and there are so many settings to change since its per rank. anyone can act like an ass, and anyone can wear poor performance avatars regardless of rank. being trusted doesnt mean anything, just makes people chase after it, uploading empty junk worlds, begging others to friend them. its all just distracting colors and separates everyone.
id like to see rank colors gone and titles at least shown only on the user's end if it really needs to be a thing, and have the performance options focus more on the details of avatars instead of the 5 tabs of rank settings

I really like the safety ranks, I just believe that it's way too easy to rank up lately. Still, they give a nice, rough estimate of playtime, which I can use to judge which kind of people I'm with.
There's no status in having "Trusted" anymore, half my friends are "veteran" in the API by now.
It has nothing to do with a "social hierarchy" for me, just that I will know whenever or not they're alright with being touched and the degree in which they know the game. Can I expect them to place a portal to a world, and to realize that they can't see another person's particle writing because of the safety setting? If they're "new user" I will try to explain these things for them. Believe it or not, the ranks are quite reliable for judging game experience.

There's more of a reason to get rid of the user ranks all together. Apparently people's accounts are now being hacked and sold to others that want a trusted user account. I'm not an expert, but this just sounds like elitism. I've also heard several stories of people in public worlds seeing other trusted users block people below their rank on sight just because of rank. And everyone I've talked to about it says that trusted users are the ones that crash people more often, which is probably because modded client users and hackers use that rank to bypass safety settings to harass people.
I feel like eventually vrchat is going to be the reason for more laws and such for online interactions.

details:
Since the section about the trust system (which contains a lot of criticism) was deleted and not restored, I decided to remind of what was previously suggested.
There is too many ranks. We have Visitor, New, User, Known and Trusted. What (more or less objective) conclusions can be drawn from these ranks, looking at an unfamiliar player:
1. Visitor -- minimum of functions.
2. New -- person can upload worlds and avatars (but not always, sometimes players don't have tags that activate the SDK)
3. User -- nothing, literally gives no information. Especially because higher ranks can disguise themselves. Can send feedback.
4. Known -- nothing new, but can be hidden.
5. Trusted -- also no new functions.
For the most part, the functional ranks are very similar to each other and are poorly distinguishable. I suggest that only 3 ranks should be:
1. Visitor -- basic access.
2. User -- plus uploading worlds, avatars and sending feedback.
3. Trusted -- plus the ability to hide and it is should be hidden by default.
Plus: In safety settings User and Trusted should have the same default settings. As we assuming Users are fully-trusted and Knowns+Trusteds are extra-trusted (with extra can be hidden), Users should not be limited by default. 
Think about it, how often did the existing gradation of ranks help you?
If you have the safety settings enabled for known or trusted, it is most likely the same for trusted or known.
How often have you noticed a difference in the behavior of new, user, and known when communicating with people? It is probably all the same. (Although it is clear that visitor and trusted are different.)
In fact, it often turns out that it is not low-ranked users who need to disable lighting and shaders, but trusted users, because they abuse the fact that they are displayed for everyone by default. Due to the large number of ranks, security management becomes more complicated, in fact, there are few functions attached to the ranks, and it is perceived by users as decor and status, resulting in an unjustified social hierarchy.
title: Too many safty ranks. Ranks are not effective and do not actually have any functionality.
